evidence.field: 考; formation and historical uses, lines 158–179
evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文’s analysis “老也。从老省，丂聲.” It favors an account in which early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; 丂 was added as a sound marker to distinguish 考, with the lower 匕 commonly omitted. It also records a competing proposal that 丂 was an original graph, proposed to depict an axe handle, used for ‘father’ before 老 was added as a semantic marker. The entry says early bronze uses of 丂 for ‘father’ give this proposal support, but favors the 老-based account for the early Western Zhou evidence. It reports named bronze examples for ‘father’ and ‘consider/estimate’, and phonetic uses for 孝 and 巧. It supplies no dates for these specific examples and does not demonstrate a semantic transition from ‘father’ to ‘examine/test’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 丂 interpretation within 昜, lines 114–124
evidence.text: The entry attributes to 屈萬里 the proposal that oracle-bone and early bronze 丂 depicts a tree branch and is an early graph for 柯. This differs from the axe-handle interpretation discussed in the 考 entry. Neither account independently establishes the original name or pronunciation of a depicted object; an object-name-based loan explanation therefore remains unverified.

evidence.text: The supplied local Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 丂 *C.qʰˤuʔ (MC khawX; gloss ‘to sob’) and 考 *k-r̥ˤuʔ (MC khawX; gloss ‘old; deceased father’). Their Old Chinese reconstructions differ, so they must not be collapsed or used alone to prove a sound relation. Local Unihan kMandarin rows give kǎo for both. Official Unicode per-character pages for U+4E02 and U+8003 were attempted but could not be opened in this session; the readings are therefore local validation, not externally verified Unihan evidence.

The official Unicode Unihan records for 考 and 丂 returned access errors, and the Baxter–Sagart PDF returned 502. Local exact rows report current Mandarin kǎo for each and distinct Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms, but these remain local checks rather than externally inspected source claims.

CUHK reports named inscription and manuscript examples for ‘father’, ‘consider/estimate’, and phonetic uses, but the inspected character-specific page gives no dates for the cited examples. Earliest attested dates remain unresolved.

The semantic development between ‘father’, ‘consider/estimate’, and current ‘examine/test’ is not established by the inspected sources. Do not infer chronology from their dictionary ordering or glosses.

The original referent and name/pronunciation of 丂 remain disputed (branch versus axe-handle interpretations, among others); a whole-graph borrowing account that depends on the depicted object’s name cannot be independently established.
The separate graphic history and chronology of 攷 relative to 考 were not investigated beyond the Ministry dictionary’s variant listing.
